title: Playing soft and dynamics in New Orleans bands
summary: Leaders cue bands to drop down quietly by signal.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: In the New Orleans bands, I know some people told me how they used to work out things playing some parts soft. And then they do it right now. Yeah, yeah, yeah. And you talk over before, the leader will tell you how to do it.

Yeah, they come solo. Sometimes the leader, he'll just say, and they just quiet right down. See? Quiet right down. You don't have to tell them nothing. Just stop right away. They watch you and they go right down. Then when you want them to come up to me, of course, you make a motion. You want them to pick up the double-folder and then they go into it. See? But then when you want your soft, that's all you do it. And they come down. I mean, that's why a fellow asked me, he said, how do you know when they're going to get soft like that? If you're watching the leader, you can't help them. You tell yourself, you tell that, you've got to come down on you. Oh, there's lots of little tricks in the bands, you know.
